newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock higher at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock higher at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordanian stocks were higher at end of weekly trade on Wednesday with healthy selective demand for industrial blue-chips and leading Arab Bank underpinning prices, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose for the third day in a row by 0.59 percent to 142.54 points from 141.70 points on Tuesday.
Dealers said the last 15 minutes of trade in key blue chips helped underpin the market in generally moderate activity with no signs of institutional buying.

Recent unrest fuelled by the government's decision this month to almost double prices of bread in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms worsened the plight of the market, already suffering from lack of cash liquidity and minimal institutional support.
The exchange's weakness sent the index below 140 points at the end of June, sliding to levels not reached since 1993.
A total of 550,443 shares changed hands on Wednesday in a moderate 596,520 dinar turnover in the cash-squeezed market.
The market was buoyed on Monday by a government pledge to encourage private sector investment and specifically a new law that would cancel a 15 percent tax levied on companies' capital increases.
Continued demand for blue-chip Arab Bank -- a major component of the official 60 share index -- helped further buttress prices, with a 2.00 dinar rise to 229 dinars.
Arab Bank, behind the market pickup in mid-week, is seen to be a main beneficiary of the new draft companies law.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- firmed 0.06 percent to 80.77 points. It was 15.43 percent down on last year.
In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories rose 10 fils to 3.370 dinars and Livestock and Poultry rose 20 fils to 550 fils on 171,278 dinar turnover.
In banks, trading was generally weak, with Islamic Bank shedding 20 fils to 3.580 fils on a turnover of 40,421 dinars.
In services, Jordan Electric Power was unchanged at 1.530 dinars and National Portfolio rose a slight 10 fils to 1.190 dinars.

Industrials dominated on Wednesday, with a 352,053 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.58 percent, banks had a 183,129 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.68 percent while services had a low 61,338 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.06 percent.
A total of 345,387 shares worth 178,245 dinars changed hands in moderate trade in the parallel market.
